sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: FACS confirmed membrane-bound surface display of the myc/GFP-tagged full-length mCD99 (L3); BiFC fluorescence demonstrated that the tagged protein retains the ability to homodimerize.
sites.rationale: L2 explicitly states the myc-tag was placed at the N-terminal end of the extracellular domain of CD99 in a full-length, membrane-anchored construct. The signal peptide spans residues 1–22 (authoritative landmarks), so the mature N-terminus is residue 23 (D); insert_after_residue = 22 is the unique junction satisfying this description. Python confirms residue 22 = P and residue 23 = D, and the tag site is 103 residues from the TM boundary (well above the ≥3 minimum). Surface display was independently confirmed by FACS anti-myc staining (L3), and dimerization function was preserved as shown by BiFC fluorescence. Full-length mCD99 BiFC constructs (mCD99-VN and mCD99-VC) expressed in COS7 cells carried a myc-tag epitope at the N-terminal end of the extracellular domain; no residue number is stated, but the signal peptide ends at residue 22 (P) and the mature N-terminus begins at residue 23 (D), making this the unique extracellular N-terminal junction.

sources.claim: The expression of the fusion proteins of the predicted sizes was verified by western blots of the transfected cells using mAb against the myc-tag epitope that was attached to the N-terminal end of the extracellular domain of CD99 (Figure 2A).

literature_notes: L1 describes the same BiFC constructs as L2/L3 but does not specify the GFP-half junction residue; it adds no independent site. L3 is corroborating functional/surface evidence for the L2 site, not a separate site. L4 (PMC12391334) reports rCD99WT-YFP and mutant variants introduced into Cd99−/− CTL cells; the naming convention (protein-YFP) and the single-pass N-out/C-in topology of CD99 place the YFP at the intracellular C-terminus (after residue 185), which is not an extracellular surface site and is therefore recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports an internal extracellular loop insertion for CD99.

literature_other_positions.note: rCD99WT-YFP and multiple mutant variants (Cyt-Mut, TM-Mut, TJ, etc.) fused YFP to the C-terminus of full-length CD99; the C-terminus (residue 185, K) is intracellular per the authoritative topology landmarks, so this is a cytoplasmic tag, not a surface tag.

BiFC constructs fused the N- and C-terminal halves of GFP (VN/VC) to full-length mCD99; with the myc-tag occupying the extracellular N-terminus (L2), the GFP halves are necessarily at the intracellular C-terminus (residue 185, K), confirmed by the single-pass N-out/C-in topology.
